newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines defers local oil price increase.
newsitem.headline: Philippines defers local oil price increase.

text.p: The Philippines' Energy Regulatory Board said on Thursday it had decided to defer an oil price increase until differences over the price-setting formula has been resolved by the justice department.
"We will put off the announcement on the oil price hike until the Department of Justice has resolved the issue," Faylona told reporters.

A congressman had questioned before the justice department the legality of the formula being used by the ERB in determining the cap of domestic oil prices. The oil companies use the cap as their selling price.
The ERB uses the previous 30-day average of the Singapore Posted Price as the basis for the price changes.

Congressman Dante Tinga further claimed the ERB erroneously raised gasoline prices by 26 centavos in September and should allow the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund to absorb that second round of increase.
On Tuesday, Faylona said the board was considering raising petroleum prices by an average of 30 centavos per litre. The price changes were supposed to take effect on Monday.
"This is a set back to our effort to deregulate the oil industry," Faylona said.
The ERB was supposed to adjust local oil prices every month based on the Singapore Posted Price. A full deregulation of the industry will be done by March next year.
Faylona did not say when the issue would be resolved.
